23762.label: Matthew 15:13
23762.text: In reply he said: “Every plant that my heavenly Father did not plant will be uprooted.

23763.label: Matthew 15:14
23763.text: Let them be. Blind guides is what they are. If, then, a blind man guides a blind man, both will fall into a pit.”

23764.label: Matthew 15:15
23764.text: Peter responded: “Make the illustration plain to us.”

23765.label: Matthew 15:16
23765.text: At this he said: “Are you also still without understanding?

23766.label: Matthew 15:17
23766.text: Are you not aware that whatever enters into the mouth passes through the stomach and is discharged into the sewer?

23767.label: Matthew 15:18
23767.text: However, whatever comes out of the mouth comes from the heart, and those things defile a man.

23768.label: Matthew 15:19
23768.text: For example, out of the heart come wicked reasonings: murders, adulteries, sexual immorality, thefts, false testimonies, blasphemies.

23769.label: Matthew 15:20
23769.text: These are the things that defile a man; but to take a meal with unwashed hands does not defile a man.”

23770.label: Matthew 15:21
23770.text: Leaving there, Jesus now went into the region of Tyre and Siʹdon.

23771.label: Matthew 15:22
23771.text: And look! a Phoe·niʹcian woman from that region came and cried out: “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David. My daughter is cruelly demon possessed.”

23772.label: Matthew 15:23
23772.text: But he did not say a word in answer to her. So his disciples came and began to urge him: “Send her away, because she keeps crying out after us.”

23773.label: Matthew 15:24
23773.text: He answered: “I was not sent to anyone except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

23774.label: Matthew 15:25
23774.text: But the woman came and did obeisance to him, saying: “Lord, help me!”

23775.label: Matthew 15:26
23775.text: In answer he said: “It is not right to take the bread of the children and throw it to the little dogs.”

23776.label: Matthew 15:27
23776.text: She said: “Yes, Lord, but really the little dogs do eat of the crumbs falling from the table of their masters.”

23777.label: Matthew 15:28
23777.text: Then Jesus replied to her: “O woman, great is your faith; let it happen to you as you wish.” And her daughter was healed from that hour on.

23778.label: Matthew 15:29
23778.text: Departing from there, Jesus next came near the Sea of Galʹi·lee, and after going up on the mountain, he was sitting there.

23779.label: Matthew 15:30
23779.text: Then large crowds approached him, bringing along people who were lame, maimed, blind, speechless, and many others, and they laid them at his feet, and he cured them.

23780.label: Matthew 15:31
23780.text: So the crowd felt amazement as they saw the speechless speaking and the maimed being made sound and the lame walking and the blind seeing, and they glorified the God of Israel.

23781.label: Matthew 15:32
23781.text: But Jesus called his disciples to him and said: “I feel pity for the crowd, because they have already stayed with me for three days and they have had nothing to eat. I do not want to send them away hungry, for they may give out on the road.”

23782.label: Matthew 15:33
23782.text: However, the disciples said to him: “Where in this isolated place are we going to get enough bread to satisfy a crowd of this size?”

23783.label: Matthew 15:34
23783.text: At this Jesus said to them: “How many loaves do you have?” They said: “Seven, and a few small fish.”

23784.label: Matthew 15:35
23784.text: So after instructing the crowd to recline on the ground,

23785.label: Matthew 15:36
23785.text: he took the seven loaves and the fish, and after offering thanks, he broke them and began giving them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds.

23786.label: Matthew 15:37
23786.text: And all ate and were satisfied, and they took up seven large baskets full of leftover fragments.

23787.label: Matthew 15:38
23787.text: Now those eating were 4,000 men, as well as women and young children.

23788.label: Matthew 15:39
23788.text: Finally, after sending the crowds away, he got into the boat and came into the region of Magʹa·dan.

23789.label: Matthew 16:1
23789.text: Here the Pharisees and Sadducees approached him, and to test him, they asked him to display to them a sign from heaven.

23790.label: Matthew 16:2
23790.text: In reply he said to them: “When evening falls, you say, ‘It will be fair weather, for the sky is fire-red,’

23791.label: Matthew 16:3
23791.text: and in the morning, ‘It will be wintry, rainy weather today, for the sky is fire-red but gloomy.’ You know how to interpret the appearance of the sky, but the signs of the times you cannot interpret.

23792.label: Matthew 16:4
23792.text: A wicked and adulterous generation keeps seeking a sign, but no sign will be given it except the sign of Joʹnah.” With that he went away, leaving them behind.

23793.label: Matthew 16:5
23793.text: Now the disciples crossed to the other side and forgot to take bread along.

23794.label: Matthew 16:6
23794.text: Jesus said to them: “Keep your eyes open and watch out for the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”

23795.label: Matthew 16:7
23795.text: So they began to reason among themselves, saying: “We did not take any loaves along.”

23796.label: Matthew 16:8
23796.text: Knowing this, Jesus said: “Why are you discussing among yourselves that you have no loaves, you with little faith?

23797.label: Matthew 16:9
23797.text: Do you not yet see the point, or do you not remember the five loaves in the case of the 5,000 and how many baskets you took up?

23798.label: Matthew 16:10
23798.text: Or the seven loaves in the case of the 4,000 and how many large baskets you took up?

23799.label: Matthew 16:11
23799.text: How is it you do not discern that I did not speak to you about bread? But watch out for the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”

23800.label: Matthew 16:12
23800.text: Then they grasped that he said to watch out, not for the leaven of bread, but for the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

23801.label: Matthew 16:13
23801.text: When he had come into the region of Caes·a·reʹa Phi·lipʹpi, Jesus asked his disciples: “Who are men saying the Son of man is?”

23802.label: Matthew 16:14
23802.text: They said: “Some say John the Baptist, others E·liʹjah, and still others Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”

23803.label: Matthew 16:15
23803.text: He said to them: “You, though, who do you say I am?”

23804.label: Matthew 16:16
23804.text: Simon Peter answered: “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”

23805.label: Matthew 16:17
23805.text: In response Jesus said to him: “Happy you are, Simon son of Joʹnah, because flesh and blood did not reveal it to you, but my Father in the heavens did.

23806.label: Matthew 16:18
23806.text: Also, I say to you: You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my congregation, and the gates of the Grave will not overpower it.

23807.label: Matthew 16:19
23807.text: I will give you the keys of the Kingdom of the heavens, and whatever you may bind on earth will already be bound in the heavens, and whatever you may loosen on earth will already be loosened in the heavens.”

23808.label: Matthew 16:20
23808.text: Then he sternly instructed the disciples not to tell anybody that he was the Christ.

23809.label: Matthew 16:21
23809.text: From that time forward, Jesus began explaining to his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders and chief priests and scribes and be killed, and on the third day be raised up.

23810.label: Matthew 16:22
23810.text: At this Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him, saying: “Be kind to yourself, Lord; you will not have this happen to you at all.”

23811.label: Matthew 16:23
23811.text: But turning his back, he said to Peter: “Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me, because you think, not God’s thoughts, but those of men.”

23812.label: Matthew 16:24
23812.text: Then Jesus said to his disciples: “If anyone wants to come after me, let him disown himself and pick up his torture stake and keep following me.

23813.label: Matthew 16:25
23813.text: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.

23814.label: Matthew 16:26
23814.text: Really, what good will it do a man if he gains the whole world but loses his life? Or what will a man give in exchange for his life?

23815.label: Matthew 16:27
23815.text: For the Son of man is to come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will repay each one according to his behavior.

23816.label: Matthew 16:28
23816.text: Truly I say to you that there are some of those standing here who will not taste death at all until first they see the Son of man coming in his Kingdom.”

23817.label: Matthew 17:1
23817.text: Six days later Jesus took Peter and James and his brother John along and led them up into a lofty mountain by themselves.

23818.label: Matthew 17:2
23818.text: And he was transfigured before them; his face shone as the sun, and his outer garments became brilliant as the light.

23819.label: Matthew 17:3
23819.text: And look! there appeared to them Moses and E·liʹjah conversing with him.

23820.label: Matthew 17:4
23820.text: Then Peter said to Jesus: “Lord, it is fine for us to be here. If you wish, I will erect three tents here, one for you, one for Moses, and one for E·liʹjah.”

23821.label: Matthew 17:5
23821.text: While he was still speaking, look! a bright cloud overshadowed them, and look! a voice out of the cloud said: “This is my Son, the beloved, whom I have approved. Listen to him.”

23822.label: Matthew 17:6
23822.text: At hearing this, the disciples fell facedown and became very much afraid.

23823.label: Matthew 17:7
23823.text: Then Jesus came near, and touching them, he said: “Get up. Have no fear.”

23824.label: Matthew 17:8
23824.text: When they looked up, they saw no one but Jesus himself.

23825.label: Matthew 17:9
23825.text: As they were descending from the mountain, Jesus commanded them: “Tell the vision to no one until the Son of man is raised up from the dead.”

23826.label: Matthew 17:10
23826.text: However, the disciples put the question to him: “Why, then, do the scribes say that E·liʹjah must come first?”

23827.label: Matthew 17:11
23827.text: In reply he said: “E·liʹjah is indeed coming and will restore all things.

23828.label: Matthew 17:12
23828.text: However, I say to you that E·liʹjah has already come, and they did not recognize him but did whatever they wanted with him. In this way also, the Son of man is going to suffer at their hands.”

23829.label: Matthew 17:13
23829.text: Then the disciples perceived that he spoke to them about John the Baptist.

23830.label: Matthew 17:14
23830.text: When they came toward the crowd, a man approached him, knelt down to him, and said:

23831.label: Matthew 17:15
23831.text: “Lord, have mercy on my son, because he is an epileptic and is ill. He falls often into the fire and often into the water.

23832.label: Matthew 17:16
23832.text: I brought him to your disciples, but they could not cure him.”

23833.label: Matthew 17:17
23833.text: In reply Jesus said: “O faithless and twisted generation, how long must I continue with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring him here to me.”

23834.label: Matthew 17:18
23834.text: Then Jesus rebuked the demon, and it came out of him, and the boy was cured from that hour.

23835.label: Matthew 17:19
23835.text: Then the disciples came to Jesus privately and said: “Why could we not expel it?”

23836.label: Matthew 17:20
23836.text: He said to them: “Because of your little faith. For truly I say to you, if you have faith the size of a mustard grain, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you.”

23838.label: Matthew 17:22
23838.text: It was while they were gathered together in Galʹi·lee that Jesus said to them: “The Son of man is going to be betrayed into men’s hands,

23839.label: Matthew 17:23
23839.text: and they will kill him, and on the third day he will be raised up.” And they were very much grieved.

23840.label: Matthew 17:24
23840.text: After they arrived in Ca·perʹna·um, the men collecting the two drachmas tax approached Peter and said: “Does your teacher not pay the two drachmas tax?”

23841.label: Matthew 17:25
23841.text: He said: “Yes.” However, when he entered the house, Jesus spoke to him first and said: “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth receive duties or head tax? From their sons or from the strangers?”

23842.label: Matthew 17:26
23842.text: When he said: “From the strangers,” Jesus said to him: “Really, then, the sons are tax-free.

23843.label: Matthew 17:27
23843.text: But that we do not cause them to stumble, go to the sea, cast a fishhook, and take the first fish that comes up, and when you open its mouth, you will find a silver coin. Take that and give it to them for me and you.”

23844.label: Matthew 18:1
23844.text: In that hour the disciples came near to Jesus and said: “Who really is greatest in the Kingdom of the heavens?”

23845.label: Matthew 18:2
23845.text: So calling a young child to him, he stood him in their midst

23846.label: Matthew 18:3
23846.text: and said: “Truly I say to you, unless you turn around and become as young children, you will by no means enter into the Kingdom of the heavens.

23847.label: Matthew 18:4
23847.text: Therefore, whoever will humble himself like this young child is the one who is the greatest in the Kingdom of the heavens;

23848.label: Matthew 18:5
23848.text: and whoever receives one such young child on the basis of my name receives me also.

23849.label: Matthew 18:6
23849.text: But whoever stumbles one of these little ones who have faith in me, it would be better for him to have hung around his neck a millstone that is turned by a donkey and to be sunk in the open sea.

23850.label: Matthew 18:7
23850.text: “Woe to the world because of the stumbling blocks! Of course, it is inevitable that stumbling blocks will come, but woe to the man through whom the stumbling block comes!

23851.label: Matthew 18:8
23851.text: If, then, your hand or your foot makes you stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter into life maimed or lame than to be thrown with two hands or two feet into the everlasting fire.

23852.label: Matthew 18:9
23852.text: Also, if your eye makes you stumble, tear it out and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter one-eyed into life than to be thrown with two eyes into the fiery Ge·henʹna.

23853.label: Matthew 18:10
23853.text: See that you do not despise one of these little ones, for I tell you that their angels in heaven always look upon the face of my Father who is in heaven.

23855.label: Matthew 18:12
23855.text: “What do you think? If a man has 100 sheep and one of them strays, will he not leave the 99 on the mountains and set out on a search for the one that is straying?

23856.label: Matthew 18:13
23856.text: And if he finds it, I certainly tell you, he rejoices more over it than over the 99 that have not strayed.

23857.label: Matthew 18:14
23857.text: Likewise, it is not a desirable thing to my Father who is in heaven for even one of these little ones to perish.

23858.label: Matthew 18:15
23858.text: “Moreover, if your brother commits a sin, go and reveal his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained your brother.

23859.label: Matthew 18:16
23859.text: But if he does not listen, take along with you one or two more, so that on the testimony of two or three witnesses every matter may be established.

23860.label: Matthew 18:17
23860.text: If he does not listen to them, speak to the congregation. If he does not listen even to the congregation, let him be to you just as a man of the nations and as a tax collector.

23861.label: Matthew 18:18
23861.text: “Truly I say to you, whatever things you may bind on earth will be things already bound in heaven, and whatever things you may loosen on earth will be things already loosened in heaven.

23862.label: Matthew 18:19
23862.text: Again I tell you truly, if two of you on earth agree concerning anything of importance that they should request, it will take place for them on account of my Father in heaven.

23863.label: Matthew 18:20
23863.text: For where there are two or three gathered together in my name, there I am in their midst.”

23864.label: Matthew 18:21
23864.text: Then Peter came and said to him: “Lord, how many times is my brother to sin against me and am I to forgive him? Up to seven times?”

23865.label: Matthew 18:22
23865.text: Jesus said to him: “I say to you, not up to seven times, but up to 77 times.

23866.label: Matthew 18:23
23866.text: “That is why the Kingdom of the heavens may be likened to a king who wanted to settle accounts with his slaves.

23867.label: Matthew 18:24
23867.text: When he started to settle them, a man was brought in who owed him 10,000 talents.

23868.label: Matthew 18:25
23868.text: But because he did not have the means to pay it back, his master ordered him and his wife and his children and all the things he owned to be sold and payment to be made.

23869.label: Matthew 18:26
23869.text: So the slave fell down and did obeisance to him, saying, ‘Be patient with me, and I will pay back everything to you.’

23870.label: Matthew 18:27
23870.text: Moved with pity at this, the master of that slave let him off and canceled his debt.

23871.label: Matthew 18:28
23871.text: But that slave went out and found one of his fellow slaves, who owed him 100 de·narʹi·i, and grabbed him and began to choke him, saying, ‘Pay back whatever you owe.’

23872.label: Matthew 18:29
23872.text: So his fellow slave fell down and began to beg him, saying, ‘Be patient with me, and I will pay you back.’

23873.label: Matthew 18:30
23873.text: However, he was not willing, but he went and had him thrown into prison until he could pay back what he owed.

23874.label: Matthew 18:31
23874.text: When his fellow slaves saw what had happened, they became greatly distressed, and they went and reported to their master all the things that had happened.

23875.label: Matthew 18:32
23875.text: Then his master summoned him and said to him: ‘Wicked slave, I canceled all that debt for you when you pleaded with me.

23876.label: Matthew 18:33
23876.text: Should you not also have shown mercy to your fellow slave as I showed mercy to you?’

23877.label: Matthew 18:34
23877.text: With that his master, provoked to wrath, handed him over to the jailers until he repaid all that he owed.

23878.label: Matthew 18:35
23878.text: My heavenly Father will also deal with you in the same way if each of you does not forgive your brother from your heart.”

23879.label: Matthew 19:1
23879.text: When Jesus had finished speaking these things, he departed from Galʹi·lee and came to the borders of Ju·deʹa across the Jordan.

23880.label: Matthew 19:2
23880.text: Also, large crowds followed him, and he cured them there.

23881.label: Matthew 19:3
23881.text: And Pharisees came to him intent on testing him, and they asked: “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife on every sort of grounds?”

23882.label: Matthew 19:4
23882.text: In reply he said: “Have you not read that the one who created them from the beginning made them male and female

23883.label: Matthew 19:5
23883.text: and said: ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and his mother and will stick to his wife, and the two will be one flesh’?

23884.label: Matthew 19:6
23884.text: So that they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore, what God has yoked together, let no man put apart.”

23885.label: Matthew 19:7
23885.text: They said to him: “Why, then, did Moses direct giving a certificate of dismissal and divorcing her?”

23886.label: Matthew 19:8
23886.text: He said to them: “Out of regard for your hard-heartedness, Moses made the concession to you of divorcing your wives, but that has not been the case from the beginning.

23887.label: Matthew 19:9
23887.text: I say to you that whoever divorces his wife, except on the grounds of sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery.”

23888.label: Matthew 19:10
23888.text: The disciples said to him: “If that is the situation of a man with his wife, it is not advisable to marry.”

23889.label: Matthew 19:11
23889.text: He said to them: “Not all men make room for the saying, but only those who have the gift.

23890.label: Matthew 19:12
23890.text: For there are eunuchs who were born that way, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men, and there are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs on account of the Kingdom of the heavens. Let the one who can make room for it make room for it.”

23891.label: Matthew 19:13
23891.text: Then young children were brought to him for him to place his hands on them and offer prayer, but the disciples reprimanded them.

23892.label: Matthew 19:14
23892.text: Jesus, however, said: “Let the young children alone, and do not try to stop them from coming to me, for the Kingdom of the heavens belongs to such ones.”

23893.label: Matthew 19:15
23893.text: And he placed his hands on them and departed from there.

23894.label: Matthew 19:16
23894.text: Now look! someone came up to him and said: “Teacher, what good must I do to gain everlasting life?”

23895.label: Matthew 19:17
23895.text: He said to him: “Why do you ask me about what is good? One there is who is good. If, though, you want to enter into life, observe the commandments continually.”

23896.label: Matthew 19:18
23896.text: He said to him: “Which ones?” Jesus said: “You must not murder, you must not commit adultery, you must not steal, you must not bear false witness,

23897.label: Matthew 19:19
23897.text: honor your father and your mother, and you must love your neighbor as yourself.”

23898.label: Matthew 19:20
23898.text: The young man said to him: “I have kept all of these; what am I still lacking?”

23899.label: Matthew 19:21
23899.text: Jesus said to him: “If you want to be perfect, go sell your belongings and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come be my follower.”

23900.label: Matthew 19:22
23900.text: When the young man heard this, he went away grieved, for he had many possessions.

23901.label: Matthew 19:23
23901.text: Then Jesus said to his disciples: “Truly I say to you that it will be difficult for a rich man to enter the Kingdom of the heavens.

23902.label: Matthew 19:24
23902.text: Again I say to you, it is easier for a camel to get through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter the Kingdom of God.”

23903.label: Matthew 19:25
23903.text: When the disciples heard that, they were greatly astounded, saying: “Who really can be saved?”

23904.label: Matthew 19:26
23904.text: Looking at them intently, Jesus said to them: “With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”

23905.label: Matthew 19:27
23905.text: Then Peter said in reply: “Look! We have left all things and followed you; what, then, will there be for us?”

23906.label: Matthew 19:28
23906.text: Jesus said to them: “Truly I say to you, in the re-creation, when the Son of man sits down on his glorious throne, you who have followed me will sit on 12 thrones, judging the 12 tribes of Israel.

23907.label: Matthew 19:29
23907.text: And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or children or lands for the sake of my name will receive a hundred times as much and will inherit everlasting life.

23908.label: Matthew 19:30
23908.text: “But many who are first will be last, and the last first.

23909.label: Matthew 20:1
23909.text: “For the Kingdom of the heavens is like the master of a house who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.

23910.label: Matthew 20:2
23910.text: After he had agreed with the workers for a de·narʹi·us a day, he sent them into his vineyard.

23911.label: Matthew 20:3
23911.text: Going out also about the third hour, he saw others standing unemployed in the marketplace;

23912.label: Matthew 20:4
23912.text: and to those he said, ‘You too go into the vineyard, and I will give you whatever is fair.’

23913.label: Matthew 20:5
23913.text: So off they went. Again he went out about the sixth hour and the ninth hour and did likewise.

23914.label: Matthew 20:6
23914.text: Finally, about the 11th hour, he went out and found others standing around, and he said to them, ‘Why have you been standing here all day unemployed?’

23915.label: Matthew 20:7
23915.text: They replied, ‘Because nobody has hired us.’ He said to them, ‘You too go into the vineyard.’

23916.label: Matthew 20:8
23916.text: “When evening came, the master of the vineyard said to his man in charge, ‘Call the workers and pay them their wages, starting with the last and ending with the first.’

23917.label: Matthew 20:9
23917.text: When the 11th-hour men came, they each received a de·narʹi·us.

23918.label: Matthew 20:10
23918.text: So when the first came, they assumed that they would receive more, but they too were paid at the rate of a de·narʹi·us.

23919.label: Matthew 20:11
23919.text: On receiving it, they began to complain against the master of the house

23920.label: Matthew 20:12
23920.text: and said, ‘These last men put in one hour’s work; still you made them equal to us who bore the burden of the day and the burning heat!’

23921.label: Matthew 20:13
23921.text: But he said in reply to one of them, ‘Fellow, I do you no wrong. You agreed with me for a de·narʹi·us, did you not?

23922.label: Matthew 20:14
23922.text: Take what is yours and go. I want to give to this last one the same as to you.

23923.label: Matthew 20:15
23923.text: Do I not have the right to do what I want with my own things? Or is your eye envious because I am good?’

23924.label: Matthew 20:16
23924.text: In this way, the last ones will be first, and the first ones last.”

23925.label: Matthew 20:17
23925.text: While going up to Jerusalem, Jesus took the 12 disciples aside privately and said to them on the road:

23926.label: Matthew 20:18
23926.text: “Look! We are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn him to death

23927.label: Matthew 20:19
23927.text: and hand him over to men of the nations to be mocked and scourged and executed on a stake; and on the third day he will be raised up.”

23928.label: Matthew 20:20
23928.text: Then the mother of the sons of Zebʹe·dee approached him with her sons, doing obeisance and asking for something from him.

23929.label: Matthew 20:21
23929.text: He said to her: “What do you want?” She replied to him: “Give the word that these two sons of mine may sit down, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your Kingdom.”

23930.label: Matthew 20:22
23930.text: Jesus answered: “You do not know what you are asking for. Can you drink the cup that I am about to drink?” They said to him: “We can.”

23931.label: Matthew 20:23
23931.text: He said to them: “You will indeed drink my cup, but to sit down at my right hand and at my left is not mine to give, but it belongs to those for whom it has been prepared by my Father.”

23932.label: Matthew 20:24
23932.text: When the ten others heard about it, they became indignant at the two brothers.

23933.label: Matthew 20:25
23933.text: But Jesus called them to him and said: “You know that the rulers of the nations lord it over them and the great men wield authority over them.

23934.label: Matthew 20:26
23934.text: This must not be the way among you; but whoever wants to become great among you must be your minister,

23935.label: Matthew 20:27
23935.text: and whoever wants to be first among you must be your slave.

23936.label: Matthew 20:28
23936.text: Just as the Son of man came, not to be ministered to, but to minister and to give his life as a ransom in exchange for many.”

23937.label: Matthew 20:29
23937.text: As they were going out of Jerʹi·cho, a large crowd followed him.

23938.label: Matthew 20:30
23938.text: And look! two blind men sitting beside the road heard that Jesus was passing by and cried out: “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!”

23939.label: Matthew 20:31
23939.text: But the crowd rebuked them, telling them to keep silent; yet they cried all the louder, saying: “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!”

23940.label: Matthew 20:32
23940.text: So Jesus stopped, called them, and said: “What do you want me to do for you?”

23941.label: Matthew 20:33
23941.text: They said to him: “Lord, let our eyes be opened.”

23942.label: Matthew 20:34
23942.text: Moved with pity, Jesus touched their eyes, and immediately they recovered their sight, and they followed him.

23943.label: Matthew 21:1
23943.text: When they got close to Jerusalem and arrived at Bethʹpha·ge on the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,

23944.label: Matthew 21:2
23944.text: saying to them: “Go into the village that is within sight, and you will at once find a donkey tied and a colt with her. Untie them and bring them to me.

23945.label: Matthew 21:3
23945.text: If someone says anything to you, you must say, ‘The Lord needs them.’ At that he will immediately send them.”

23946.label: Matthew 21:4
23946.text: This actually took place to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet, who said:

23947.label: Matthew 21:5
23947.text: “Tell the daughter of Zion: ‘Look! Your king is coming to you, mild-tempered and mounted on a donkey, yes, on a colt, the offspring of a beast of burden.’”

23948.label: Matthew 21:6
23948.text: So the disciples went and did just as Jesus had instructed them.

23949.label: Matthew 21:7
23949.text: They brought the donkey and its colt, and they put their outer garments on them, and he sat on them.

23950.label: Matthew 21:8
23950.text: Most of the crowd spread their outer garments on the road, while others were cutting down branches from the trees and spreading them on the road.

23951.label: Matthew 21:9
23951.text: Moreover, the crowds going ahead of him and those following him kept shouting: “Save, we pray, the Son of David! Blessed is the one who comes in Jehovah’s name! Save him, we pray, in the heights above!”

23952.label: Matthew 21:10
23952.text: And when he entered Jerusalem, the whole city was in an uproar, saying: “Who is this?”

23953.label: Matthew 21:11
23953.text: The crowds kept saying: “This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazʹa·reth of Galʹi·lee!”

23954.label: Matthew 21:12
23954.text: Jesus entered the temple and threw out all those selling and buying in the temple, and he overturned the tables of the money changers and the benches of those selling doves.

23955.label: Matthew 21:13
23955.text: And he said to them: “It is written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer,’ but you are making it a cave of robbers.”

23956.label: Matthew 21:14
23956.text: Also, blind and lame people came to him in the temple, and he cured them.

23957.label: Matthew 21:15
23957.text: When the chief priests and the scribes saw the marvelous things he did and the boys who were shouting in the temple, “Save, we pray, the Son of David!” they became indignant

23958.label: Matthew 21:16
23958.text: and said to him: “Do you hear what these are saying?” Jesus said to them: “Yes. Did you never read this, ‘Out of the mouth of children and infants, you have brought forth praise’?”

23959.label: Matthew 21:17
23959.text: And leaving them behind, he went out of the city to Bethʹa·ny and spent the night there.

23960.label: Matthew 21:18
23960.text: While returning to the city early in the morning, he felt hungry.

23961.label: Matthew 21:19
23961.text: He caught sight of a fig tree by the road and went to it, but he found nothing on it except leaves, and he said to it: “Let no fruit come from you ever again.” And the fig tree withered instantly.

23962.label: Matthew 21:20
23962.text: When the disciples saw this, they were amazed and said: “How is it that the fig tree withered instantly?”

23963.label: Matthew 21:21
23963.text: In answer Jesus said to them: “Truly I say to you, if you have faith and do not doubt, not only will you do what I did to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ it will happen.

23964.label: Matthew 21:22
23964.text: And all the things you ask in prayer, having faith, you will receive.”

23965.label: Matthew 21:23
23965.text: After he went into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came up to him while he was teaching and said: “By what authority do you do these things? And who gave you this authority?”

23966.label: Matthew 21:24
23966.text: In reply Jesus said to them: “I will also ask you one thing. If you tell me, then I will also tell you by what authority I do these things:

23967.label: Matthew 21:25
23967.text: The baptism by John, from what source was it? From heaven or from men?” But they began to reason among themselves, saying: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say to us, ‘Why, then, did you not believe him?’

23968.label: Matthew 21:26
23968.text: But if we say, ‘From men,’ we have the crowd to fear, for they all regard John as a prophet.”

23969.label: Matthew 21:27
23969.text: So they answered Jesus: “We do not know.” He, in turn, said to them: “Neither am I telling you by what authority I do these things.

23970.label: Matthew 21:28
23970.text: “What do you think? A man had two children. Going up to the first, he said, ‘Child, go work today in the vineyard.’

23971.label: Matthew 21:29
23971.text: In answer this one said, ‘I will not,’ but afterward, he felt regret and went out.

23972.label: Matthew 21:30
23972.text: Approaching the second, he said the same. This one replied, ‘I will, Sir,’ but did not go out.

23973.label: Matthew 21:31
23973.text: Which of the two did the will of his father?” They said: “The first.” Jesus said to them: “Truly I say to you that the tax collectors and the prostitutes are going ahead of you into the Kingdom of God.

23974.label: Matthew 21:32
23974.text: For John came to you in a way of righteousness, but you did not believe him. However, the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him, and even when you saw this, you did not feel regret afterward so as to believe him.

23975.label: Matthew 21:33
23975.text: “Hear another illustration: There was a man, a landowner, who planted a vineyard and put a fence around it and dug a winepress in it and erected a tower; then he leased it to cultivators and traveled abroad.

23976.label: Matthew 21:34
23976.text: When the fruit season came around, he sent his slaves to the cultivators to collect his fruit.

23977.label: Matthew 21:35
23977.text: However, the cultivators took his slaves, and they beat one up, another they killed, another they stoned.

23978.label: Matthew 21:36
23978.text: Again he sent other slaves, more than the first group, but they did the same to these.

23979.label: Matthew 21:37
23979.text: Lastly he sent his son to them, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’

23980.label: Matthew 21:38
23980.text: On seeing the son, the cultivators said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and get his inheritance!’

23981.label: Matthew 21:39
23981.text: So they took him and threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.

23982.label: Matthew 21:40
23982.text: Therefore, when the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those cultivators?”

23983.label: Matthew 21:41
23983.text: They said to him: “Because they are evil, he will bring a terrible destruction on them and will lease the vineyard to other cultivators, who will give him the fruits when they become due.”

23984.label: Matthew 21:42
23984.text: Jesus said to them: “Did you never read in the Scriptures, ‘The stone that the builders rejected, this has become the chief cornerstone. This has come from Jehovah, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?

23985.label: Matthew 21:43
23985.text: This is why I say to you, the Kingdom of God will be taken from you and be given to a nation producing its fruits.

23986.label: Matthew 21:44
23986.text: Also, the person falling on this stone will be shattered. As for anyone on whom it falls, it will crush him.”

23987.label: Matthew 21:45
23987.text: When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his illustrations, they knew that he was speaking about them.

23988.label: Matthew 21:46
23988.text: Although they wanted to seize him, they feared the crowds, because these regarded him as a prophet.

23989.label: Matthew 22:1
23989.text: Once more Jesus spoke to them with illustrations, saying:

23990.label: Matthew 22:2
23990.text: “The Kingdom of the heavens may be likened to a king who made a marriage feast for his son.

23991.label: Matthew 22:3
23991.text: And he sent his slaves to call those invited to the marriage feast, but they were unwilling to come.

23992.label: Matthew 22:4
23992.text: Again he sent other slaves, saying, ‘Tell those invited: “Look! I have prepared my dinner, my bulls and fattened animals are slaughtered, and everything is ready. Come to the marriage feast.”’

23993.label: Matthew 22:5
23993.text: But unconcerned they went off, one to his own field, another to his business;

23994.label: Matthew 22:6
23994.text: but the rest, seizing his slaves, treated them insolently and killed them.

23995.label: Matthew 22:7
23995.text: “The king grew wrathful and sent his armies and killed those murderers and burned their city.

23996.label: Matthew 22:8
23996.text: Then he said to his slaves, ‘The marriage feast is ready, but those invited were not worthy.

23997.label: Matthew 22:9
23997.text: Therefore, go to the roads leading out of the city, and invite anyone you find to the marriage feast.’

23998.label: Matthew 22:10
23998.text: Accordingly, those slaves went out to the roads and gathered all they found, both wicked and good; and the room for the wedding ceremonies was filled with those dining.

23999.label: Matthew 22:11
23999.text: “When the king came in to inspect the guests, he caught sight of a man not wearing a marriage garment.

24000.label: Matthew 22:12
24000.text: So he said to him, ‘Fellow, how did you get in here without a marriage garment?’ He was speechless.

24001.label: Matthew 22:13
24001.text: Then the king said to his servants, ‘Bind him hand and foot and throw him into the darkness outside. There is where his weeping and the gnashing of his teeth will be.’

24002.label: Matthew 22:14
24002.text: “For there are many invited, but few chosen.”

24003.label: Matthew 22:15
24003.text: Then the Pharisees went and conspired together in order to trap him in his speech.

24004.label: Matthew 22:16
24004.text: So they sent their disciples to him, together with party followers of Herod, saying: “Teacher, we know you are truthful and teach the way of God in truth, and you do not seek anyone’s favor, for you do not look at the outward appearance of people.

24005.label: Matthew 22:17
24005.text: Tell us, then, what do you think? Is it lawful to pay head tax to Caesar or not?”

24006.label: Matthew 22:18
24006.text: But Jesus, knowing their wickedness, said: “Why do you put me to the test, hypocrites?

24007.label: Matthew 22:19
24007.text: Show me the tax coin.” They brought him a de·narʹi·us.

24008.label: Matthew 22:20
24008.text: He said to them: “Whose image and inscription is this?”

24009.label: Matthew 22:21
24009.text: They said: “Caesar’s.” Then he said to them: “Pay back, therefore, Caesar’s things to Caesar, but God’s things to God.”

24010.label: Matthew 22:22
24010.text: When they heard that, they were amazed, and they left him and went away.

24011.label: Matthew 22:23
24011.text: On that day the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came and asked him:

24012.label: Matthew 22:24
24012.text: “Teacher, Moses said: ‘If any man dies without having children, his brother must marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’

24013.label: Matthew 22:25
24013.text: Now there were seven brothers with us. The first married and died, and having no offspring, he left his wife for his brother.

24014.label: Matthew 22:26
24014.text: The same thing happened with the second and the third, through all seven.

24015.label: Matthew 22:27
24015.text: Last of all, the woman died.

24016.label: Matthew 22:28
24016.text: So in the resurrection, of the seven, whose wife will she be? For they all had her as a wife.”

24017.label: Matthew 22:29
24017.text: In reply Jesus said to them: “You are mistaken, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God;

24018.label: Matthew 22:30
24018.text: for in the resurrection neither do men marry nor are women given in marriage, but they are as angels in heaven.

24019.label: Matthew 22:31
24019.text: Regarding the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what was spoken to you by God, who said:

24020.label: Matthew 22:32
24020.text: ‘I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob’? He is the God, not of the dead, but of the living.”

24021.label: Matthew 22:33
24021.text: On hearing that, the crowds were astounded at his teaching.

24022.label: Matthew 22:34
24022.text: After the Pharisees heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, they came together in one group.

24023.label: Matthew 22:35
24023.text: And one of them, versed in the Law, tested him by asking:

24024.label: Matthew 22:36
24024.text: “Teacher, which is the greatest commandment in the Law?”

24025.label: Matthew 22:37
24025.text: He said to him: “‘You must love Jehovah your God with your whole heart and with your whole soul and with your whole mind.’

24026.label: Matthew 22:38
24026.text: This is the greatest and first commandment.

24027.label: Matthew 22:39
24027.text: The second, like it, is this: ‘You must love your neighbor as yourself.’

24028.label: Matthew 22:40
24028.text: On these two commandments the whole Law hangs, and the Prophets.”

24029.label: Matthew 22:41
24029.text: Now while the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them:

24030.label: Matthew 22:42
24030.text: “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he?” They said to him: “David’s.”

24031.label: Matthew 22:43
24031.text: He asked them: “How is it, then, that David under inspiration calls him Lord, saying,

24032.label: Matthew 22:44
24032.text: ‘Jehovah said to my Lord: “Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies beneath your feet”’?

24033.label: Matthew 22:45
24033.text: If, then, David calls him Lord, how is he his son?”

24034.label: Matthew 22:46
24034.text: And nobody was able to say a word in reply to him, and from that day on, no one dared to question him any further.

24035.label: Matthew 23:1
24035.text: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to his disciples, saying:

24036.label: Matthew 23:2
24036.text: “The scribes and the Pharisees have seated themselves in the seat of Moses.

24037.label: Matthew 23:3
24037.text: Therefore, all the things they tell you, do and observe, but do not do according to their deeds, for they say but they do not practice what they say.

24038.label: Matthew 23:4
24038.text: They bind up heavy loads and put them on the shoulders of men, but they themselves are not willing to budge them with their finger.

24039.label: Matthew 23:5
24039.text: All the works they do, they do to be seen by men, for they broaden the scripture-containing cases that they wear as safeguards and lengthen the fringes of their garments.

24040.label: Matthew 23:6
24040.text: They like the most prominent place at evening meals and the front seats in the synagogues

24041.label: Matthew 23:7
24041.text: and the greetings in the marketplaces and to be called Rabbi by men.

24042.label: Matthew 23:8
24042.text: But you, do not you be called Rabbi, for one is your Teacher, and all of you are brothers.

24043.label: Matthew 23:9
24043.text: Moreover, do not call anyone your father on earth, for one is your Father, the heavenly One.

24044.label: Matthew 23:10
24044.text: Neither be called leaders, for your Leader is one, the Christ.

24045.label: Matthew 23:11
24045.text: But the greatest one among you must be your minister.

24046.label: Matthew 23:12
24046.text: Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

24047.label: Matthew 23:13
24047.text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you shut up the Kingdom of the heavens before men; for you yourselves do not go in, neither do you permit those on their way in to go in.

24049.label: Matthew 23:15
24049.text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you travel over sea and dry land to make one proselyte, and when he becomes one, you make him a subject for Ge·henʹna twice as much so as yourselves.

24050.label: Matthew 23:16
24050.text: “Woe to you, blind guides, who say, ‘If anyone swears by the temple, it is nothing; but if anyone swears by the gold of the temple, he is under obligation.’

24051.label: Matthew 23:17
24051.text: Fools and blind ones! Which, in fact, is greater, the gold or the temple that has sanctified the gold?

24052.label: Matthew 23:18
24052.text: Moreover, ‘If anyone swears by the altar, it is nothing; but if anyone swears by the gift on it, he is under obligation.’

24053.label: Matthew 23:19
24053.text: Blind ones! Which, in fact, is greater, the gift or the altar that sanctifies the gift?

24054.label: Matthew 23:20
24054.text: Therefore, whoever swears by the altar is swearing by it and by all the things on it;

24055.label: Matthew 23:21
24055.text: and whoever swears by the temple is swearing by it and by the One inhabiting it;

24056.label: Matthew 23:22
24056.text: and whoever swears by heaven is swearing by the throne of God and by the One sitting on it.

24057.label: Matthew 23:23
24057.text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you give the tenth of the mint and the dill and the cumin, but you have disregarded the weightier matters of the Law, namely, justice and mercy and faithfulness. These things it was necessary to do, yet not to disregard the other things.

24058.label: Matthew 23:24
24058.text: Blind guides, who strain out the gnat but gulp down the camel!

24059.label: Matthew 23:25
24059.text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you cleanse the outside of the cup and of the dish, but inside they are full of greediness and self-indulgence.

24060.label: Matthew 23:26
24060.text: Blind Pharisee, cleanse first the inside of the cup and of the dish, so that the outside of it may also become clean.

24061.label: Matthew 23:27
24061.text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you resemble whitewashed graves, which outwardly indeed appear beautiful but inside are full of dead men’s bones and of every sort of uncleanness.

24062.label: Matthew 23:28
24062.text: In the same way, on the outside you appear righteous to men, but inside you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.

24063.label: Matthew 23:29
24063.text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you build the graves of the prophets and decorate the tombs of the righteous ones,

24064.label: Matthew 23:30
24064.text: and you say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our forefathers, we would not have shared with them in shedding the blood of the prophets.’

24065.label: Matthew 23:31
24065.text: Therefore, you are testifying against yourselves that you are sons of those who murdered the prophets.

24066.label: Matthew 23:32
24066.text: Well, then, fill up the measure of your forefathers.

24067.label: Matthew 23:33
24067.text: “Serpents, offspring of vipers, how will you flee from the judgment of Ge·henʹna?

24068.label: Matthew 23:34
24068.text: For this reason, I am sending to you prophets and wise men and public instructors. Some of them you will kill and execute on stakes, and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues and persecute from city to city,

24069.label: Matthew 23:35
24069.text: so that there may come upon you all the righteous blood spilled on earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zech·a·riʹah son of Bar·a·chiʹah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar.

24070.label: Matthew 23:36
24070.text: Truly I say to you, all these things will come upon this generation.

24071.label: Matthew 23:37
24071.text: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the killer of the prophets and stoner of those sent to her —how often I wanted to gather your children together the way a hen gathers her chicks under her wings! But you did not want it.

24072.label: Matthew 23:38
24072.text: Look! Your house is abandoned to you.

24073.label: Matthew 23:39
24073.text: For I say to you, you will by no means see me from now until you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in Jehovah’s name!’”

24074.label: Matthew 24:1
24074.text: Now as Jesus was departing from the temple, his disciples approached to show him the buildings of the temple.

24075.label: Matthew 24:2
24075.text: In response he said to them: “Do you not see all these things? Truly I say to you, by no means will a stone be left here upon a stone and not be thrown down.”

24076.label: Matthew 24:3
24076.text: While he was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples approached him privately, saying: “Tell us, when will these things be, and what will be the sign of your presence and of the conclusion of the system of things?”

24077.label: Matthew 24:4
24077.text: In answer Jesus said to them: “Look out that nobody misleads you,

24078.label: Matthew 24:5
24078.text: for many will come on the basis of my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will mislead many.

24079.label: Matthew 24:6
24079.text: You are going to hear of wars and reports of wars. See that you are not alarmed, for these things must take place, but the end is not yet.

24080.label: Matthew 24:7
24080.text: “For nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be food shortages and earthquakes in one place after another.

24081.label: Matthew 24:8
24081.text: All these things are a beginning of pangs of distress.

24082.label: Matthew 24:9
24082.text: “Then people will hand you over to tribulation and will kill you, and you will be hated by all the nations on account of my name.

24083.label: Matthew 24:10
24083.text: Then, too, many will be stumbled and will betray one another and will hate one another.

24084.label: Matthew 24:11
24084.text: Many false prophets will arise and mislead many;

24085.label: Matthew 24:12
24085.text: and because of the increasing of lawlessness, the love of the greater number will grow cold.

24086.label: Matthew 24:13
24086.text: But the one who has endured to the end will be saved.

24087.label: Matthew 24:14
24087.text: And this good news of the Kingdom will be preached in all the inhabited earth for a witness to all the nations, and then the end will come.

24088.label: Matthew 24:15
24088.text: “Therefore, when you catch sight of the disgusting thing that causes desolation, as spoken about by Daniel the prophet, standing in a holy place (let the reader use discernment),

24089.label: Matthew 24:16
24089.text: then let those in Ju·deʹa begin fleeing to the mountains.

24090.label: Matthew 24:17
24090.text: Let the man on the housetop not come down to take the goods out of his house,

24091.label: Matthew 24:18
24091.text: and let the man in the field not return to pick up his outer garment.

24092.label: Matthew 24:19
24092.text: Woe to the pregnant women and those nursing a baby in those days!

24093.label: Matthew 24:20
24093.text: Keep praying that your flight may not occur in wintertime nor on the Sabbath day;

24094.label: Matthew 24:21
24094.text: for then there will be great tribulation such as has not occurred since the world’s beginning until now, no, nor will occur again.

24095.label: Matthew 24:22
24095.text: In fact, unless those days were cut short, no flesh would be saved; but on account of the chosen ones those days will be cut short.

24096.label: Matthew 24:23
24096.text: “Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look! Here is the Christ,’ or, ‘There!’ do not believe it.

24097.label: Matthew 24:24
24097.text: For false Christs and false prophets will arise and will perform great signs and wonders so as to mislead, if possible, even the chosen ones.

24099.label: Matthew 24:26
24099.text: Therefore, if people say to you, ‘Look! He is in the wilderness,’ do not go out; ‘Look! He is in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.

24100.label: Matthew 24:27
24100.text: For just as the lightning comes out of the east and shines over to the west, so the presence of the Son of man will be.

24101.label: Matthew 24:28
24101.text: Wherever the carcass is, there the eagles will be gathered together.

24102.label: Matthew 24:29
24102.text: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

24103.label: Matthew 24:30
24103.text: Then the sign of the Son of man will appear in heaven, and all the tribes of the earth will beat themselves in grief, and they will see the Son of man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.

24104.label: Matthew 24:31
24104.text: And he will send out his angels with a great trumpet sound, and they will gather his chosen ones together from the four winds, from one extremity of the heavens to their other extremity.

24105.label: Matthew 24:32
24105.text: “Now learn this illustration from the fig tree: Just as soon as its young branch grows tender and sprouts its leaves, you know that summer is near.

24106.label: Matthew 24:33
24106.text: Likewise also you, when you see all these things, know that he is near at the doors.

24107.label: Matthew 24:34
24107.text: Truly I say to you that this generation will by no means pass away until all these things happen.

24108.label: Matthew 24:35
24108.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will by no means pass away.

24109.label: Matthew 24:36
24109.text: “Concerning that day and hour nobody knows, neither the angels of the heavens nor the Son, but only the Father.

24110.label: Matthew 24:37
24110.text: For just as the days of Noah were, so the presence of the Son of man will be.

24111.label: Matthew 24:38
24111.text: For as they were in those days before the Flood, eating and drinking, men marrying and women being given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ark,

24112.label: Matthew 24:39
24112.text: and they took no note until the Flood came and swept them all away, so the presence of the Son of man will be.

24113.label: Matthew 24:40
24113.text: Then two men will be in the field; one will be taken along and the other abandoned.

24114.label: Matthew 24:41
24114.text: Two women will be grinding at the hand mill; one will be taken along and the other abandoned.

24115.label: Matthew 24:42
24115.text: Keep on the watch, therefore, because you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.

24116.label: Matthew 24:43
24116.text: “But know one thing: If the householder had known in what watch the thief was coming, he would have kept awake and not allowed his house to be broken into.

24117.label: Matthew 24:44
24117.text: On this account, you too prove yourselves ready, because the Son of man is coming at an hour that you do not think to be it.

24118.label: Matthew 24:45
24118.text: “Who really is the faithful and discreet slave whom his master appointed over his domestics, to give them their food at the proper time?

24119.label: Matthew 24:46
24119.text: Happy is that slave if his master on coming finds him doing so!

24120.label: Matthew 24:47
24120.text: Truly I say to you, he will appoint him over all his belongings.

24121.label: Matthew 24:48
24121.text: “But if ever that evil slave says in his heart, ‘My master is delaying,’

24122.label: Matthew 24:49
24122.text: and he starts to beat his fellow slaves and to eat and drink with the confirmed drunkards,

24123.label: Matthew 24:50
24123.text: the master of that slave will come on a day that he does not expect and in an hour that he does not know,

24124.label: Matthew 24:51
24124.text: and he will punish him with the greatest severity and will assign him his place with the hypocrites. There is where his weeping and the gnashing of his teeth will be.

24125.label: Matthew 25:1
24125.text: “Then the Kingdom of the heavens may be likened to ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.

24126.label: Matthew 25:2
24126.text: Five of them were foolish, and five were discreet.

24127.label: Matthew 25:3
24127.text: For the foolish took their lamps but took no oil with them,

24128.label: Matthew 25:4
24128.text: whereas the discreet took oil in their flasks along with their lamps.

24129.label: Matthew 25:5
24129.text: While the bridegroom was delaying, they all became drowsy and fell asleep.

24130.label: Matthew 25:6
24130.text: Right in the middle of the night there was a shout: ‘Here is the bridegroom! Go out to meet him.’

24131.label: Matthew 25:7
24131.text: Then all those virgins got up and put their lamps in order.

24132.label: Matthew 25:8
24132.text: The foolish said to the discreet, ‘Give us some of your oil, because our lamps are about to go out.’

24133.label: Matthew 25:9
24133.text: The discreet answered, saying: ‘Perhaps there may not be enough for both us and you. Go instead to those who sell it, and buy some for yourselves.’

24134.label: Matthew 25:10
24134.text: While they were going off to buy it, the bridegroom came. The virgins who were ready went in with him to the marriage feast, and the door was shut.

24135.label: Matthew 25:11
24135.text: Afterward, the rest of the virgins also came, saying, ‘Sir, Sir, open to us!’

24136.label: Matthew 25:12
24136.text: In answer he said, ‘I tell you the truth, I do not know you.’

24137.label: Matthew 25:13
24137.text: “Keep on the watch, therefore, because you know neither the day nor the hour.

24138.label: Matthew 25:14
24138.text: “For it is just like a man about to travel abroad who summoned his slaves and entrusted his belongings to them.

24139.label: Matthew 25:15
24139.text: He gave five talents to one, two to another, and one to still another, to each according to his own ability, and he went abroad.

24140.label: Matthew 25:16
24140.text: Immediately the one who received the five talents went and did business with them and gained five more.

24141.label: Matthew 25:17
24141.text: Likewise, the one who received the two gained two more.

24142.label: Matthew 25:18
24142.text: But the slave who received just one went off and dug in the ground and hid his master’s money.

24143.label: Matthew 25:19
24143.text: “After a long time, the master of those slaves came and settled accounts with them.

24144.label: Matthew 25:20
24144.text: So the one who had received the five talents came forward and brought five additional talents, saying, ‘Master, you entrusted five talents to me; see, I gained five talents more.’

24145.label: Matthew 25:21
24145.text: His master said to him: ‘Well done, good and faithful slave! You were faithful over a few things. I will appoint you over many things. Enter into the joy of your master.’

24146.label: Matthew 25:22
24146.text: Next the one who had received the two talents came forward and said, ‘Master, you entrusted two talents to me; see, I gained two talents more.’

24147.label: Matthew 25:23
24147.text: His master said to him: ‘Well done, good and faithful slave! You were faithful over a few things. I will appoint you over many things. Enter into the joy of your master.’

24148.label: Matthew 25:24
24148.text: “Finally the slave who had received the one talent came forward and said: ‘Master, I knew you to be a demanding man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering where you did not winnow.

24149.label: Matthew 25:25
24149.text: So I grew afraid and went and hid your talent in the ground. Here, you have what is yours.’

24150.label: Matthew 25:26
24150.text: In reply his master said to him: ‘Wicked and sluggish slave, you knew, did you, that I reaped where I did not sow and gathered where I did not winnow?

24151.label: Matthew 25:27
24151.text: Well, then, you should have deposited my money with the bankers, and on my coming I would have received it back with interest.

24152.label: Matthew 25:28
24152.text: “‘Therefore, take the talent away from him and give it to the one who has the ten talents.

24153.label: Matthew 25:29
24153.text: For to everyone who has, more will be given, and he will have an abundance. But the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.

24154.label: Matthew 25:30
24154.text: And throw the good-for-nothing slave out into the darkness outside. There is where his weeping and the gnashing of his teeth will be.’

24155.label: Matthew 25:31
24155.text: “When the Son of man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, then he will sit down on his glorious throne.

24156.label: Matthew 25:32
24156.text: All the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate people one from another, just as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.

24157.label: Matthew 25:33
24157.text: And he will put the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on his left.

24158.label: Matthew 25:34
24158.text: “Then the King will say to those on his right: ‘Come, you who have been blessed by my Father, inherit the Kingdom prepared for you from the founding of the world.

24159.label: Matthew 25:35
24159.text: For I became hungry and you gave me something to eat; I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink. I was a stranger and you received me hospitably;

24160.label: Matthew 25:36
24160.text: naked and you clothed me. I fell sick and you looked after me. I was in prison and you visited me.’

24161.label: Matthew 25:37
24161.text: Then the righteous ones will answer him with the words: ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you something to drink?

24162.label: Matthew 25:38
24162.text: When did we see you a stranger and receive you hospitably, or naked and clothe you?

24163.label: Matthew 25:39
24163.text: When did we see you sick or in prison and visit you?’

24164.label: Matthew 25:40
24164.text: In reply the King will say to them, ‘Truly I say to you, to the extent that you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.’

24165.label: Matthew 25:41
24165.text: “Then he will say to those on his left: ‘Go away from me, you who have been cursed, into the everlasting fire prepared for the Devil and his angels.

24166.label: Matthew 25:42
24166.text: For I became hungry, but you gave me nothing to eat; and I was thirsty, but you gave me nothing to drink.

24167.label: Matthew 25:43
24167.text: I was a stranger, but you did not receive me hospitably; naked, but you did not clothe me; sick and in prison, but you did not look after me.’

24168.label: Matthew 25:44
24168.text: Then they too will answer with the words: ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison and did not minister to you?’

24169.label: Matthew 25:45
24169.text: Then he will answer them, saying: ‘Truly I say to you, to the extent that you did not do it to one of these least ones, you did not do it to me.’

24170.label: Matthew 25:46
24170.text: These will depart into everlasting cutting-off, but the righteous ones into everlasting life.”

24171.label: Matthew 26:1
24171.text: Now when Jesus had finished saying all these things, he said to his disciples:

24172.label: Matthew 26:2
24172.text: “You know that two days from now the Passover takes place, and the Son of man will be handed over to be executed on the stake.”

24173.label: Matthew 26:3
24173.text: Then the chief priests and the elders of the people gathered in the courtyard of the high priest, who was named Caʹia·phas,

24174.label: Matthew 26:4
24174.text: and they conspired together to seize Jesus by cunning and to kill him.

24175.label: Matthew 26:5
24175.text: However, they were saying: “Not at the festival, so that there may not be an uproar among the people.”

24176.label: Matthew 26:6
24176.text: While Jesus was in Bethʹa·ny in the house of Simon the leper,

24177.label: Matthew 26:7
24177.text: a woman with an alabaster jar of costly perfumed oil approached him, and she began pouring it on his head as he was dining.

24178.label: Matthew 26:8
24178.text: On seeing this, the disciples became indignant and said: “Why this waste?

24179.label: Matthew 26:9
24179.text: For this could have been sold for a great deal of money and given to the poor.”

24180.label: Matthew 26:10
24180.text: Aware of this, Jesus said to them: “Why do you try to make trouble for the woman? She did a fine deed toward me.

24181.label: Matthew 26:11
24181.text: For you always have the poor with you, but you will not always have me.

24182.label: Matthew 26:12
24182.text: When she put this perfumed oil on my body, she did it to prepare me for burial.

24183.label: Matthew 26:13
24183.text: Truly I say to you, wherever this good news is preached in all the world, what this woman did will also be told in memory of her.”

24184.label: Matthew 26:14
24184.text: Then one of the Twelve, the one called Judas Is·carʹi·ot, went to the chief priests

24185.label: Matthew 26:15
24185.text: and said: “What will you give me to betray him to you?” They stipulated to him 30 silver pieces.

24186.label: Matthew 26:16
24186.text: So from then on, he kept looking for a good opportunity to betray him.

24187.label: Matthew 26:17
24187.text: On the first day of the Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus, saying: “Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?”

24188.label: Matthew 26:18
24188.text: He said: “Go into the city to So-and-so and say to him, ‘The Teacher says: “My appointed time is near; I will celebrate the Passover with my disciples at your home.”’”

24189.label: Matthew 26:19
24189.text: So the disciples did as Jesus instructed them and prepared for the Passover.

24190.label: Matthew 26:20
24190.text: When evening came, he was reclining at the table with the 12 disciples.

24191.label: Matthew 26:21
24191.text: While they were eating, he said: “Truly I say to you, one of you will betray me.”

24192.label: Matthew 26:22
24192.text: Being very much grieved at this, each and every one began to say to him: “Lord, it is not I, is it?”

24193.label: Matthew 26:23
24193.text: In reply he said: “The one who dips his hand with me into the bowl is the one who will betray me.

24194.label: Matthew 26:24
24194.text: True, the Son of man is going away, just as it is written about him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of man is betrayed! It would have been better for that man if he had not been born.”

24195.label: Matthew 26:25
24195.text: Judas, who was about to betray him, replied: “It is not I, is it, Rabbi?” Jesus said to him: “You yourself said it.”

24196.label: Matthew 26:26
24196.text: As they continued eating, Jesus took a loaf, and after saying a blessing, he broke it, and giving it to the disciples, he said: “Take, eat. This means my body.”

24197.label: Matthew 26:27
24197.text: And taking a cup, he offered thanks and gave it to them, saying: “Drink out of it, all of you,

24198.label: Matthew 26:28
24198.text: for this means my ‘blood of the covenant,’ which is to be poured out in behalf of many for forgiveness of sins.

24199.label: Matthew 26:29
24199.text: But I say to you: I will by no means drink again any of this product of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in the Kingdom of my Father.”

24200.label: Matthew 26:30
24200.text: Finally, after singing praises, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

24201.label: Matthew 26:31
24201.text: Then Jesus said to them: “All of you will be stumbled in connection with me on this night, for it is written: ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered about.’

24202.label: Matthew 26:32
24202.text: But after I have been raised up, I will go ahead of you into Galʹi·lee.”

24203.label: Matthew 26:33
24203.text: But Peter, in response, said to him: “Although all the others are stumbled in connection with you, I will never be stumbled!”

24204.label: Matthew 26:34
24204.text: Jesus said to him: “Truly I say to you, on this night, before a rooster crows, you will disown me three times.”

24205.label: Matthew 26:35
24205.text: Peter said to him: “Even if I should have to die with you, I will by no means disown you.” All the other disciples also said the same thing.

24206.label: Matthew 26:36
24206.text: Then Jesus came with them to the spot called Geth·semʹa·ne, and he said to the disciples: “Sit down here while I go over there and pray.”

24207.label: Matthew 26:37
24207.text: And taking along Peter and the two sons of Zebʹe·dee, he began to feel grieved and to be greatly troubled.

24208.label: Matthew 26:38
24208.text: Then he said to them: “I am deeply grieved, even to death. Stay here and keep on the watch with me.”

24209.label: Matthew 26:39
24209.text: And going a little way forward, he fell facedown, praying: “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from me. Yet, not as I will, but as you will.”

24210.label: Matthew 26:40
24210.text: He returned to the disciples and found them sleeping, and he said to Peter: “Could you not so much as keep on the watch for one hour with me?

24211.label: Matthew 26:41
24211.text: Keep on the watch and pray continually, so that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit, of course, is eager, but the flesh is weak.”

24212.label: Matthew 26:42
24212.text: Again, a second time, he went off and prayed: “My Father, if it is not possible for this to pass away unless I drink it, let your will take place.”

24213.label: Matthew 26:43
24213.text: And he came again and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.

24214.label: Matthew 26:44
24214.text: So leaving them, he again went off and prayed for a third time, saying once more the same thing.

24215.label: Matthew 26:45
24215.text: Then he returned to the disciples and said to them: “At such a time as this, you are sleeping and resting! Look! The hour has drawn near for the Son of man to be betrayed into the hands of sinners.

24216.label: Matthew 26:46
24216.text: Get up, let us go. Look! My betrayer has drawn near.”

24217.label: Matthew 26:47
24217.text: While he was still speaking, look! Judas, one of the Twelve, came and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests and the elders of the people.

24218.label: Matthew 26:48
24218.text: Now his betrayer had given them a sign, saying: “Whoever it is I kiss, he is the one; take him into custody.”

24219.label: Matthew 26:49
24219.text: And going straight up to Jesus, he said: “Greetings, Rabbi!” and gave him a tender kiss.

24220.label: Matthew 26:50
24220.text: But Jesus said to him: “Fellow, for what purpose are you present?” Then they came forward and seized Jesus and took him into custody.

24221.label: Matthew 26:51
24221.text: But look! one of those with Jesus reached out his hand and drew his sword and struck the slave of the high priest, taking off his ear.

24222.label: Matthew 26:52
24222.text: Then Jesus said to him: “Return your sword to its place, for all those who take up the sword will perish by the sword.

24223.label: Matthew 26:53
24223.text: Or do you think that I cannot appeal to my Father to supply me at this moment more than 12 legions of angels?

24224.label: Matthew 26:54
24224.text: In that case, how would the Scriptures be fulfilled that say it must take place this way?”

24225.label: Matthew 26:55
24225.text: In that hour Jesus said to the crowds: “Did you come out to arrest me with swords and clubs as against a robber? Day after day I used to sit in the temple teaching, and yet you did not take me into custody.

24226.label: Matthew 26:56
24226.text: But all of this has taken place for the writings of the prophets to be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples abandoned him and fled.

24227.label: Matthew 26:57
24227.text: Those who took Jesus into custody led him away to Caʹia·phas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were gathered together.

24228.label: Matthew 26:58
24228.text: But Peter kept following him from a good distance, as far as the courtyard of the high priest, and after going inside, he sat with the house attendants to see the outcome.

24229.label: Matthew 26:59
24229.text: Now the chief priests and the entire Sanʹhe·drin were looking for false testimony against Jesus in order to put him to death.

24230.label: Matthew 26:60
24230.text: But they found none, although many false witnesses came forward. Later two came forward

24231.label: Matthew 26:61
24231.text: and said: “This man said, ‘I am able to throw down the temple of God and build it up in three days.’”

24232.label: Matthew 26:62
24232.text: With that the high priest stood up and said to him: “Do you say nothing in reply? What is it these men are testifying against you?”

24233.label: Matthew 26:63
24233.text: But Jesus kept silent. So the high priest said to him: “I put you under oath by the living God to tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God!”

24234.label: Matthew 26:64
24234.text: Jesus said to him: “You yourself said it. But I say to you: From now on you will see the Son of man sitting at the right hand of power and coming on the clouds of heaven.”

24235.label: Matthew 26:65
24235.text: Then the high priest ripped his outer garments, saying: “He has blasphemed! What further need do we have of witnesses? See! Now you have heard the blasphemy.

24236.label: Matthew 26:66
24236.text: What is your opinion?” They answered: “He deserves to die.”

24237.label: Matthew 26:67
24237.text: Then they spat in his face and hit him with their fists. Others slapped him on the face,

24238.label: Matthew 26:68
24238.text: saying: “Prophesy to us, you Christ. Who struck you?”

24239.label: Matthew 26:69
24239.text: Now Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and a servant girl came up to him and said: “You too were with Jesus the Gal·i·leʹan!”

24240.label: Matthew 26:70
24240.text: But he denied it before them all, saying: “I do not know what you are talking about.”

24241.label: Matthew 26:71
24241.text: When he went out to the gatehouse, another girl noticed him and said to those there: “This man was with Jesus the Naz·a·reneʹ.”

24242.label: Matthew 26:72
24242.text: Again he denied it, with an oath: “I do not know the man!”

24243.label: Matthew 26:73
24243.text: After a little while, those standing around came up and said to Peter: “Certainly you are also one of them, for in fact, your dialect gives you away.”

24244.label: Matthew 26:74
24244.text: Then he started to curse and swear: “I do not know the man!” And immediately a rooster crowed.

24245.label: Matthew 26:75
24245.text: And Peter called to mind what Jesus had said, namely: “Before a rooster crows, you will disown me three times.” And he went outside and wept bitterly.

24246.label: Matthew 27:1
24246.text: When morning came, all the chief priests and the elders of the people consulted together against Jesus to put him to death.

24247.label: Matthew 27:2
24247.text: After binding him, they led him off and handed him over to Pilate, the governor.

24248.label: Matthew 27:3
24248.text: Then Judas, his betrayer, seeing that Jesus had been condemned, felt remorse and brought the 30 pieces of silver back to the chief priests and elders,

24249.label: Matthew 27:4
24249.text: saying: “I sinned when I betrayed innocent blood.” They said: “What is that to us? You must see to it!”

24250.label: Matthew 27:5
24250.text: So he threw the silver pieces into the temple and departed. Then he went off and hanged himself.

24251.label: Matthew 27:6
24251.text: But the chief priests took the silver pieces and said: “It is not lawful to put them into the sacred treasury, because they are the price of blood.”

24252.label: Matthew 27:7
24252.text: After consulting together, they used the money to buy the potter’s field as a burial place for strangers.

24253.label: Matthew 27:8
24253.text: Therefore, that field has been called Field of Blood to this very day.

24254.label: Matthew 27:9
24254.text: Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled: “And they took the 30 silver pieces, the price that was set on the man, the one on whom a price was set by some of the sons of Israel,

24255.label: Matthew 27:10
24255.text: and they gave them for the potter’s field, according to what Jehovah had commanded me.”

24256.label: Matthew 27:11
24256.text: Jesus now stood before the governor, and the governor put the question to him: “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus replied: “You yourself say it.”

24257.label: Matthew 27:12
24257.text: But while he was being accused by the chief priests and elders, he made no answer.

24258.label: Matthew 27:13
24258.text: Then Pilate said to him: “Do you not hear how many things they are testifying against you?”

24259.label: Matthew 27:14
24259.text: But he did not answer him, no, not a word, so that the governor was very surprised.

24260.label: Matthew 27:15
24260.text: Now from festival to festival, it was the custom of the governor to release a prisoner to the crowd, whomever they wanted.

24261.label: Matthew 27:16
24261.text: Just at that time they were holding a notorious prisoner called Bar·abʹbas.

24262.label: Matthew 27:17
24262.text: So when they were gathered together, Pilate said to them: “Which one do you want me to release to you, Bar·abʹbas or Jesus the so-called Christ?”

24263.label: Matthew 27:18
24263.text: For Pilate was aware that out of envy they had handed him over.

24264.label: Matthew 27:19
24264.text: Moreover, while he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent a message to him, saying: “Have nothing to do with that righteous man, for I suffered a lot today in a dream because of him.”

24265.label: Matthew 27:20
24265.text: But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Bar·abʹbas, but to have Jesus put to death.

24266.label: Matthew 27:21
24266.text: In response the governor said to them: “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?” They said: “Bar·abʹbas.”

24267.label: Matthew 27:22
24267.text: Pilate said to them: “What, then, should I do with Jesus the so-called Christ?” They all said: “To the stake with him!”

24268.label: Matthew 27:23
24268.text: He said: “Why? What bad thing did he do?” Still they kept shouting out all the more: “To the stake with him!”

24269.label: Matthew 27:24
24269.text: Seeing that it did no good but, rather, an uproar was arising, Pilate took water and washed his hands before the crowd, saying: “I am innocent of the blood of this man. You yourselves must see to it.”

24270.label: Matthew 27:25
24270.text: At that all the people said in answer: “Let his blood come upon us and upon our children.”

24271.label: Matthew 27:26
24271.text: Then he released Bar·abʹbas to them, but he had Jesus whipped and handed him over to be executed on the stake.

24272.label: Matthew 27:27
24272.text: Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the governor’s residence and gathered the whole body of troops together around him.

24273.label: Matthew 27:28
24273.text: And disrobing him, they draped him with a scarlet cloak,

24274.label: Matthew 27:29
24274.text: and they braided a crown out of thorns and put it on his head and put a reed in his right hand. And kneeling before him, they mocked him, saying: “Greetings, you King of the Jews!”

24275.label: Matthew 27:30
